Landing in power-darkness (screening risk HIGH): the visible solar disk is below the panel threshold at landing and stays so for 63 h from landing. The lander would depend on stored energy, which is not modelled.

Landing without Earth line of sight (screening risk HIGH): Earth is obstructed at landing and stays so for 136 h from landing. Direct-to-Earth contact is geometrically impossible until Earth reappears; relays are not modelled.

Real NASA-derived geometry with terrain horizons: dataset 'connecting-ridge_2026-01-01_2031-01-01', generator 'Member 1 precompute (backend/scripts/precompute.py), generator_version 1.2'. Results inherit the accuracy and resolution of the ephemeris and elevation data and change when the data are regenerated; keep the dataset id and generator with any stored result.
Sun and Earth states are known for the whole 336 h evaluated range (336 samples); no result depends on missing data.

Time resolution: samples are up to 1 h apart (sample-hold, no interpolation). Transition times are resolved only to that spacing, shorter events can be missed, and smaller duration margins are not resolved.

Sunlight here is geometric visibility of the solar disk, not electrical power: array orientation, efficiency, temperature, dust, batteries and the power system are not modelled. 'Power-lit' only means the visible disk fraction meets the configured panel threshold.
Earth line of sight is a geometric opportunity, not guaranteed communication: antenna pointing, link budget, ground-station availability, relays and interference are not modelled.

Spacecraft limits (maximum darkness and blackout durations, panel threshold) are used as configured and are not verified: battery capacity, thermal survival and radio hardware are not modelled. Nothing here assesses landing safety (slopes, hazards).
Risk headroom bands (10 % HIGH, 25 % MODERATE by default) are product-defined screening heuristics, not NASA-certified safety thresholds, and no probability of mission failure is computed.

assumptions: Sample-and-hold: each instantaneous sample represents [t_i, t_(i+1)) when the next sample is within sampling.max_gap_s (5400 s); before a coverage gap and at the last sample it represents one nominal interval (3600 s), never beyond coverage_end_utc. Modeled transitions fall on sample times and can be up to one sample spacing later than the true geometric event.
No interpolation between samples; events shorter than the sample spacing can be missed.
Unknown states and time no sample represents are never treated as darkness or blackout; affected durations, percentages and outages are reported as bounds.
Percentages use the whole evaluated range as denominator; means are time-weighted.

limitations: Solar illumination is not electrical power generation; array orientation, efficiency, temperature, dust and power-system design are not modelled.
Earth line of sight is not guaranteed radio connectivity; antenna pointing, link budget, ground-station availability and interference are not modelled.
Viability covers illumination and direct-to-Earth line of sight under the stated constraints only; it is not an assessment of landing safety (slopes, hazards, terrain).
Terrain-aware results inherit the resolution and accuracy of the elevation model and horizon calculation; geometric-only results ignore terrain entirely.
Sampled time series can miss events shorter than the sampling interval.

ranking_status.rule: Only rank_eligible assessments (eligibility PASS) receive a rank. UNKNOWN is neither scored nor ranked; FAIL keeps a descriptive score but is never ranked against viable scenarios. A bounded score is an interval, never a point value, and a missing score is never zero. Assessments may share one ranking only if their comparability fields are all equal (data_basis, scoring_method_version, effective_weights and, under the strict policy, configuration_key).

explanation.message: Sun and Earth states are known for the whole 336 h evaluated range (336 samples); no result depends on missing data.

details: sun_data_coverage (low): Sun state is known for the whole mission (336 h).
earth_data_coverage (low): Earth state is known for the whole mission (336 h).

explanation.message: Time resolution: samples are up to 1 h apart (sample-hold, no interpolation). Transition times are resolved only to that spacing, shorter events can be missed, and smaller duration margins are not resolved.

details: assumption: Sample-and-hold: each instantaneous sample represents [t_i, t_(i+1)) when the next sample is within sampling.max_gap_s (5400 s); before a coverage gap and at the last sample it represents one nominal interval (3600 s), never beyond coverage_end_utc. Modeled transitions fall on sample times and can be up to one sample spacing later than the true geometric event.
assumption: No interpolation between samples; events shorter than the sample spacing can be missed.
assumption: Unknown states and time no sample represents are never treated as darkness or blackout; affected durations, percentages and outages are reported as bounds.
assumption: Percentages use the whole evaluated range as denominator; means are time-weighted.

explanation.message: Sunlight here is geometric visibility of the solar disk, not electrical power: array orientation, efficiency, temperature, dust, batteries and the power system are not modelled. 'Power-lit' only means the visible disk fraction meets the configured panel threshold.

details: Solar illumination is not electrical power generation; array orientation, efficiency, temperature, dust and power-system design are not modelled.

explanation.message: Earth line of sight is a geometric opportunity, not guaranteed communication: antenna pointing, link budget, ground-station availability, relays and interference are not modelled.

details: Earth line of sight is not guaranteed radio connectivity; antenna pointing, link budget, ground-station availability and interference are not modelled.

explanation.message: Spacecraft limits (maximum darkness and blackout durations, panel threshold) are used as configured and are not verified: battery capacity, thermal survival and radio hardware are not modelled. Nothing here assesses landing safety (slopes, hazards).

details: Viability covers illumination and direct-to-Earth line of sight under the stated constraints only; it is not an assessment of landing safety (slopes, hazards, terrain).
Terrain-aware results inherit the resolution and accuracy of the elevation model and horizon calculation; geometric-only results ignore terrain entirely.
Sampled time series can miss events shorter than the sampling interval.

explanation.message: Risk headroom bands (10 % HIGH, 25 % MODERATE by default) are product-defined screening heuristics, not NASA-certified safety thresholds, and no probability of mission failure is computed.

details: Bands apply to headroom = margin / reference; see each indicator's rule for the policy used.
